question.prompt:
Two opposite sides of a rectangle are each divided into \(n\) congruent segments, and the endpoints of one segment are joined to the center to form triangle \(A.\) The other sides are each divided into \(m\) congruent segments, and the endpoints of one of these segments are joined to the center to form triangle \(B.\) [See figure for \(n=5,\) \(m=7.\)] What is the ratio of the area of triangle \(A\) to the area of triangle \(B?\)

[Figure 1](figures/1996_AMC_12_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The center is halfway between each pair of opposite sides. This makes each triangle's height half the rectangle's dimension perpendicular to its base.

Let the rectangle have width \(w>0\) and height \(h>0\), with the sides of length \(h\) divided into \(n\) equal segments. Here \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. Triangle \(A\) has base \(h/n\) and perpendicular height \(w/2\), so its area is
\[
S_A=\frac12\cdot\frac{h}{n}\cdot\frac{w}{2}
=\frac{wh}{4n}.
\]
The other pair of sides has length \(w\). Triangle \(B\) therefore has base \(w/m\) and height \(h/2\), giving
\[
S_B=\frac12\cdot\frac{w}{m}\cdot\frac{h}{2}
=\frac{wh}{4m}.
\]
Both areas are positive, so their ratio is defined. The common rectangle dimensions cancel:
\[
\frac{S_A}{S_B}
=\frac{wh}{4n}\cdot\frac{4m}{wh}
=\boxed{\frac{m}{n}}.
\]
Thus the answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the base-height products
